Crossover est le podcast d'Urban Comics,: Crossover is the podcast of Urban Comics, the French publisher of DC, Vertigo and the Energon Universe. It's hosted by Frédérick Sigrist — the man behind Blockbusters, which we dissected in episode 6. Launched in 2023, it has 43 episodes. The principle fits in its slogan: one month, one podcast, one genre.
Chaque épisode réunit un plateau à trois: Each episode brings together a three-way panel: a bookseller, a journalist or influencer, and an Urban editor. Sigrist isn't a presenter dropped onto a catalogue: he has always taken popular culture seriously, and he asks a reader's questions, not a PR person's. Themes range from the Batman-Superman-Wonder Woman trinity to the Elseworlds, by way of Zorro, Dracula and the Universal Monsters, or Jack Kirby's Fourth World.
Bruce Wayne sort d'une projection de Zor: Bruce Wayne is coming out of a Zorro screening the night his parents are killed. Devoting an episode to Zorro is the choice of a podcast that knows its classics — and the one that tells you straight away whether it's serious.
Et si Superman s'était écrasé en Union s: What if Superman had crash-landed in the Soviet Union? What if Batman had crossed paths with Jack the Ripper? The finest concept in American publishing, explained to those who've never come across it.
Avec Philippe Peythieu, la voix français: With Philippe Peythieu, the French voice of Homer Simpson. Ask anyone to name the best Joker: they'll answer with a voice. It's the most accessible episode, even if you've never opened a comic.
La question qui fâche saute aux yeux : U: The awkward question jumps out: Urban Comics produces a podcast about comics published by Urban Comics, with an Urban editor on the panel. Content, or a catalogue with music? Our answer: transparency saves everything. Nothing is hidden, it's in the title, nobody is fooled. And the panel includes a bookseller and a journalist, two people with no reason to lie about a book — a bookseller who recommends a bad album pays for it at the counter the following week. It's passion funded by someone with an interest in it existing, which has nothing to do with disguised advertising.
Deux réserves et une demie. Le rythme :: Two and a half reservations. The pace: one episode a month on a subject that moves every week, between releases, films and series — you always feel you've arrived after the party. The scope: the title promises "all the worlds of American comics", but it's very largely the DC universe and the Urban catalogue. Logical, they're their books; if you're after Marvel, you'll be waiting a long time. To start, take the French dubbing episode, then the New Gods to understand where half of modern pop culture comes from.
